t: You're in the area of St Ann Blackfriars, a church that stood in what is now Ireland Yard, in the City of London. It began as a medieval parish chapel within the Dominicans' church. After Henry VIII dissolved the monastery, a parish church was set up in the sixteenth century for the people living in its precincts. It stood near the Blackfriars Theatre, which displeased its congregation, and it was destroyed in the Great Fire of 1666. Samuel Bradford, later bishop of Carlisle and then Rochester, was born here in 1652.
